title: Distributed Two-Phase Commit (2PC) Blocking Coordinator Failure
pattern: A distributed transaction participant (cohort) votes "yes" to prepare a write, but the coordinator crashes before sending the final "commit" or "abort" decision.
why_bad: Because 2PC is a blocking protocol, the cohort is left indefinitely in-doubt, holding lock resources on its local database forever and preventing subsequent queries from executing.
detection: Implementation of standard distributed 2PC where participant nodes block indefinitely on resource locks without a fallback consensus recovery protocol or transaction manager timeout resolution.
counterexample: Using decentralized consensus algorithms (such as Paxos, Raft, or RAMP) or 3-Phase Commit (3PC) which resolve in-doubt participants on timeouts.
fix: Migrate from a standard blocking 2PC to a decentralized consensus algorithm (such as Paxos, Raft, or RAMP) or use a three-phase commit (3PC) with participant-side timeouts.
